name: Engineering
description: Electrical, mechanical, civil and computer engineering: circuits, signals, structures, machines, control.

figureTypes.name: Circuit schematic
figureTypes.description: Code-drawn schematic with labeled components and node voltages.

figureTypes.name: Plot from equations or data
figureTypes.description: Line plot of a verified equation or dataset, key points labeled directly.

figureTypes.name: Block diagram
figureTypes.description: Signal or system flow, left to right.

figureTypes.name: Free-body diagram
figureTypes.description: Forces as arrows from the body, with magnitudes and angles.

figureTypes.name: Bode plot
figureTypes.description: Magnitude (dB) and phase versus log frequency.

conventions: Use SI units with SI prefixes: 4.7 kΩ, 100 nF, 1.6 ms.
Put a space between number and unit (10 V), except for degrees of angle (90°).
Write the unit name in words the first time it appears in a chapter: 10 µF (microfarads).
Frequency f is in hertz (Hz); angular frequency ω is in radians per second (rad/s). Never mix them without the 2π.

safetyNotes: Experiments in this book use low voltages (under 30 V). Mains voltage and large charged capacitors can injure or kill; do not build mains-powered circuits without training and supervision.
restrictedDetail: Designs whose main purpose is to harm people or disable safety systems
Step-by-step instructions for high-energy discharge devices
draftingNotes: Every circuit example must use component values a student can buy (E12/E24 resistor series, common capacitor values).
State whether a model is ideal (zero wire resistance, ideal capacitor) and what a real part does differently.
